newsitem.title: PERU: Peruvian hostages suffering ill health - Red Cross.
newsitem.headline: Peruvian hostages suffering ill health - Red Cross.

text.p: Hostages held by leftist guerrillas inside the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima since Tuesday are suffering from ill health and overcrowding, the Red Cross said on Friday.

"The situation inside is difficult. There is overcrowding, it is very hot," Red Cross official Sergio Natarajan said after visiting the nearly 400 hostages with a doctor and a nurse. "Among the illnesses are diabetes, ulcers, heart problems and diarrhoea."

The Red Cross, which is leading negotiations between the Peruvian government and about 20 rebels of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA), had previously been relatively positive about the condition of the hostages.
The captives, all men, have now spent three nights sleeping on the floor in cramped conditions, dressed in the elegant clothes worn to Tuesday evening's cocktail party at the residence.
Natarajan said the Red Cross would continue supplying the hostages with basic needs such as food and water in an effort to ease their discomfort.
He added that some family members had offered to swap with ill relatives inside the residence. "But we are not going to get involved in that matter," he said.
